chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

Na'fi ibn al-Azraq asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Inform me about Allah - when was He? He (the Imam) said to him: Woe be upon you! You inform me when wasn't He, then I will inform you when He was. Glory be to the One who has always been and will always be Singular, Eternal, not taking a partner nor offspring.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), referring to Imam al-Baqir

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic theological understanding of Allah's eternity and timelessness?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Abu Hamza al-Thumali, illustrates the Shia theological concept of Allah's transcendence over temporal constraints (Zaman). By asking 'when were you not?', Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates that time is a created attribute, whereas Allah's existence is necessary and eternal (Qadim). The concluding phrase 'Sahiban wa Walada' echoes the Quranic rejection of physical lineage, reinforcing the doctrine of Tawhid al-Asma wa al-Sifat.
